title: Toys from Trash: Air and Water
desc: A menu of low-cost air and water experiments made from scrap, such as a cloth siphon, balloon diver, water lens, smoke rings, hot air balloon, water wheel, fun fountain and two-bottle fountain.
how: Pick one build a week; each needs only bottles, straws, balloons and similar household junk.

title: Toys from Trash: Electricity and Magnetism
desc: A long list of electricity and magnet toys to build, including a potato battery, salt-water battery, electric swing, magnetic levitation, maglev train, magnetic field lines and static charge bending water.
how: Good for a magnets or circuits unit; an adult should help with batteries and wire stripping.

title: Toys from Trash: Spinning Toys
desc: Hundreds of spinners, tops and fans made from household scrap, such as a coin spinner, buddy top, square paper spinner and simple top.
how: Use while teaching pushes, pulls and how things move; younger children can make paper spinners alone.

title: Toys from Trash: Flying Toys
desc: Children make and fly paper toys like a paper helicopter, flying fish, jumping dragonfly, catapult parachute, flying disc, styrofoam glider and balloon rocket.
how: Fly them from a height and compare which fall slowest to talk about air resistance and gravity.

title: Toys from Trash: Fun with Light
desc: Light projects made from card and mirror pieces, including a simple periscope, a pinhole camera, total reflection and invisible glass.
how: Pair the periscope and pinhole camera with lessons on light travelling in straight lines.

title: Toys from Trash: Simple Sounds
desc: Homemade instruments and noisemakers such as a balloon bugle, straw whistles, a singing pipe and a roaring cup; cutting straws to different lengths changes the pitch.
how: Make two or three and let the child explain why each one sounds higher or lower.

title: Toys from Trash: Beginner's Biology
desc: Paper and scrap models of the body, including a skeleton from A4 paper, inflatable lungs, a folding paper heart, human body systems and the digestive system.
how: Build the model while reading the body chapter so the child can point to each part.

title: Human Digestive System model
desc: A Toys from Trash model page for making a model of the human digestive system from simple materials.
how: Use alongside the digestion chapter; trace the path food takes on the finished model.

title: Arvind Gupta free science toy films
desc: Short one- to two-minute films showing how to make and play with science toys, such as a simple motor, magnetic levitation pencil, LED torch, balancing toys and a brain cap, in English and several Indian languages.
how: Let the child watch a film in their home language, then build the toy straight after.

title: A Revolutionary Motor
desc: Step-by-step sheet for building a working electric motor from a torch battery, a ferrite magnet, two safety pins, rubber bands and copper wire; flipping the magnet reverses the spin.
how: A weekend build with adult help; ask the child to predict what happens when the magnet is turned over.

title: An Electrifying Life: Michael Faraday
desc: Arvind Gupta's article on Michael Faraday with builds inspired by him: an electromagnet made by winding wire on a steel nail and a syringe generator that lights an LED when shaken.
how: Read the story first, then make the nail electromagnet together.

title: Science Skills and Thrills
desc: A free booklet of Arvind Gupta's best simple science toys, such as a spinner and a toothpick merry-go-round that turns when you blow through a pen refill.
how: Keep it as a rainy-day book of quick builds.

title: Toy Treasures
desc: A free book of simple toys with instructions, including a flying fish made from a strip of newspaper and a helicopter made from a postcard and paper clip.
how: Good first builds for younger children with little adult help.

title: Ten Little Fingers: Ideas and Activities in Science
desc: Simple science ideas for young children, such as collecting nuts, seeds and leaves and using them for pattern-making and a bingo-style game.
how: For 6-8 year olds; start with a nature walk to collect seeds and leaves.

title: Toys from Trash (full collection)
desc: The index of Arvind Gupta's 700+ science toys made from junk, grouped by topic, each with photos and clear instructions.
how: Browse by topic to find a toy for whatever chapter the child is on.

title: Amazing Kitchen Chemistry Projects
desc: A free book of chemistry projects children do in the kitchen with everyday ingredients, hosted on Arvind Gupta's site.
how: Pick projects with an adult at the stove; good for a changing-materials unit.

title: Science Experiments with Paper
source: Steven W. Moje, hosted by Arvind Gupta Toys
desc: Experiments using only paper, including a 'flying things' section with a weighted spinning paper plate, an index-card helicopter and a paper aeroplane, explaining how shape and wings affect flight.
how: Cheap to run at home; pair with the flying toys page.

title: Mirrors: Finding Out About the Properties of Light
source: Bernie Zubrowski, hosted by Arvind Gupta Toys
desc: Mirror activities and games, such as one where a 'seeker' lines up four mirrors to see a 'hider' at the other end of the table.
how: Needs a few small mirrors; good for two or more children.

title: Physics Experiments for Children
source: Muriel Mandell, hosted by Arvind Gupta Toys
desc: A free book of simple physics experiments, including showing how shadows are formed and building a periscope.
how: Use the light and shadow experiments during a light unit.

title: 700 Science Experiments for Everyone
source: UNESCO, hosted by Arvind Gupta Toys
desc: UNESCO's classic collection of 700 simple science experiments using everyday materials.
how: A reference book for parents to pick experiments for any topic.

title: Toying Around with Science
source: Bob Friedhoffer, hosted by Arvind Gupta Toys
desc: Explains the physics behind toys, for example why a spinning gyroscope is easier to balance.
how: Mainly for the parent or an older child, to explain why the toys they build work.

title: Human Body Systems
desc: A reference text on human body systems, covering how the heart and lungs work and how oxygen passes from the air into the blood.
how: For older children; read alongside the inflatable lungs and paper heart models.

title: Common Trees of India
desc: A free book about the common trees of India, for learning to recognise the trees around you.
how: Take it on walks to identify neighbourhood trees; pairs well with SeasonWatch.

title: Plant Myths and Traditions in India
source: Shakti M. Gupta, hosted by Arvind Gupta Toys
desc: A book on myths and traditions linked to plants in India.
how: For the parent to read and retell; links plants to the festivals and customs children see.

title: Brahma's Hair: On the Mythology of Indian Plants
source: Maneka Gandhi and Yasmin Singh, hosted by Arvind Gupta Toys
desc: A book of myths and stories about Indian plants and trees.
how: Pick a tree from the neighbourhood and read its story together.

title: Fun with Water
source: Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (TIFR), Small Science
desc: Water activities to build, such as a water turbine, a water wheel, a simple rain gauge, a submarine and a fun fountain, credited to arvindguptatoys.com.
how: Make the rain gauge in the monsoon and record rainfall for a week.

title: StoryWeaver Science storybooks
desc: Free illustrated science picture books to read online or download, such as The Case of the Missing Water, Ammachi's Amazing Machines and A Butterfly Smile, many in several Indian languages.
how: Choose a book in the child's home language for bedtime reading on the week's topic.

title: StoryWeaver National Science Day STEM books
desc: StoryWeaver's post introducing its non-fiction science picture books on robotics, measurement, genes and forest canopies, made in 10 languages.
how: Parents use it to find the books, especially the one on genes.

title: Anna's Extraordinary Experiments with Weather
source: Pratham Books (StoryWeaver), via Free Kids Books
desc: A picture-book biography of Indian meteorologist Anna Mani, who as a child wanted books instead of diamond earrings and grew up to study the weather.
how: Read it when talking about weather and seasons, or about Indian scientists.

title: SeasonWatch
desc: Children register a tree near home, check it every week and record whether it has fresh or mature leaves, buds, flowers, and unripe or ripe fruit; casual one-time observations are also possible.
how: Adopt one tree for a year; it turns seasons and plant life cycles into something the child sees.

title: The Calendar of Nature: SeasonWatch handbook
desc: SeasonWatch's project handbook for schools on tracking the seasons through weekly observations of trees.
how: Read it first to learn how to record a tree before joining SeasonWatch.

title: Great Backyard Bird Count (India)
desc: Every February, families watch birds for four days, list the birds they see (for example every 15 minutes) and upload the lists to eBird; the pages also share India's results each year.
how: Mark mid-February on the calendar and do a 15-minute count from home or a park each day.

title: Campus Bird Count stories: children at Isha Home School
desc: An account of 24 children who were paired up, given areas of their campus and listed birds every 15 minutes, submitting about 200 checklists of more than 100 species.
how: Read it before your own bird count to show how children do it.

title: ISRO for Students
desc: ISRO's student portal with a space quiz, knowledge videos, ISRO missions at a glance, a space dictionary and a link to the virtual museum.
how: Try the quiz after a unit on the sky and space.

title: SPARK: ISRO's virtual space museum
desc: A 3D virtual space park to walk around online, with a museum, a theatre playing space videos, an observatory, a garden of life-sized rockets and a children's play area.
how: Explore it together on a computer; look for the rockets and satellites that carry signals around the world.

title: Vigyan Prasar Earthquake Kit
desc: A hands-on kit with activities such as making a model seismological observatory, a slinky demonstration of seismic waves and flip books on fault types, with the book 'Earthquakes'.
how: A paid kit; worth buying for a group or a learning pod.

title: Vigyan Prasar activity kits
desc: Low-cost hands-on science kits built from locally available materials, including an astronomy kit with about 30 activities and a chemistry kit with 45 activities.
how: Paid kits to buy from Vigyan Prasar; the astronomy kit suits a sky unit.

title: ePathshala: NCERT textbooks and e-resources
desc: NCERT's free portal with all Class 1-12 textbooks as digital books, including the Class 3-5 EVS and science books, plus audios, videos, interactives, images and maps; the mobile app can read textbooks aloud.
how: Use it to read the NCERT chapter itself, for example Family and Friends or Going to the Mela in Class 3.
